{{Short description|Mathematical sequence of integers}}
{{More footnotes|date=April 2025}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Genocchi numbers''' G<sub>''n''</sub>, named after [[Angelo Genocchi]], are a [[sequence (mathematics)|sequence]] of [[integer]]s  that satisfy the relation

:<math>
\frac{2t}{1+e^{t}}=\sum_{n=0}^\infty G_n\frac{t^n}{n!}
</math>

The first few Genocchi numbers are 0, 1, &minus;1, 0, 1, 0, &minus;3, 0, 17 {{OEIS|id=A226158}}, see {{OEIS2C|id=A001469}}.

:<math>
G_n=2(1-2^n)(-n\zeta(1-n)),
</math><ref>{{cite web|title=An Introduction to the Bernoulli Function|publisher=arXiv preprint|last=Luschny|first=Peter H. N.|url=https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.06743|year=2020}}</ref>
where <math>\zeta(1-n)</math> is the [[Riemann zeta function]].
== Properties ==

* The [[generating function]] definition of the Genocchi numbers implies that they are [[rational number]]s. In fact, G<sub>''2n+1''</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 for ''n''&nbsp;&ge;&nbsp;1 and (&minus;1)<sup>''n''</sup>G<sub>''2n''</sub> is an [[odd number|odd]] positive integer.
* Genocchi numbers ''G''<sub>''n''</sub> are related to [[Bernoulli numbers]] ''B''<sub>''n''</sub> by the formula

: <math>
 G_{n}=2 \,(1-2^n) \,B_n.
</math>

== Combinatorial interpretations ==

The [[exponential generating function]] for the '''signed even Genocchi numbers''' (&minus;1)<sup>''n''</sup>G<sub>''2n''</sub> is 
:<math>
 t\tan \left(\frac{t}{2} \right)=\sum_{n\geq 1} (-1)^n G_{2n}\frac{t^{2n}}{(2n)!}
</math>

They enumerate the following objects:

* [[Permutation]]s in ''S''<sub>2''n''&minus;1</sub> with [[Permutation#Descents|descents]] after the even numbers and [[Permutation#Descents|ascents]] after the odd numbers.
* Permutations ''&pi;'' in ''S''<sub>2''n''&minus;2</sub> with 1&nbsp;&le;&nbsp;''&pi;''(2''i''&minus;1)&nbsp;&le;&nbsp;2''n''&minus;2''i'' and 2''n''&minus;2''i''&nbsp;&le;&nbsp;''&pi;''(2''i'')&nbsp;&le;&nbsp;2''n''&minus;2.
* Pairs (''a''<sub>1</sub>,...,''a''<sub>''n''&minus;1</sub>) and (''b''<sub>1</sub>,...,''b''<sub>''n''&minus;1</sub>) such that ''a''<sub>''i''</sub> and ''b''<sub>''i''</sub> are between 1 and ''i'' and every ''k'' between 1 and ''n''&minus;1 occurs at least once among the ''a''<sub>''i''</sub>'s and ''b''<sub>''i''</sub>'s.
* Reverse [[alternating permutation]]s ''a''<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;<&nbsp;''a''<sub>2</sub>&nbsp;>&nbsp;''a''<sub>3</sub>&nbsp;<&nbsp;''a''<sub>4</sub>&nbsp;>...>''a''<sub>2''n''&minus;1</sub> of [2''n''&minus;1] whose [[Permutation#Numbering permutations|inversion table]] has only even entries.

== Primes ==
The only known prime numbers which occur in the Genocchi sequence are 17, at n = 8, and −3, at n = 6 (depending on how primes are defined). It has been proven that no other primes occur in the sequence
